auxiliary.task: from the GRU state predict whether the safe gap's screen-x centre lies left or right of x=192; label = round21.telegraph_gap(s), i.e. s.gap under s.mirror
auxiliary.supervision_window: the rows whose logical frame 2*i lies inside round21.telegraph_window(s) = [wall_frame-45, wall_frame)
auxiliary.head: Linear(256, 2, bias=True) outside `heads`
auxiliary.parent_detach: inert: the auxiliary head is downstream of the GRU, so no line of the parent body is overridden
auxiliary.inference: the closed loop builds a plain TacticalPolicy from payload["heads"]; the auxiliary state is never loaded and there is no module to hold it

features.note: the 94-d spatial vector that function also returns is not used; it is the frozen proof that the encode pass is round22's

intervention.note: the only change against round22 is the auxiliary head on the GRU state and its loss weight; arm A is round22 A with that weight at zero

storage.dtype: uint8 (the renderer output verbatim, never cast to float on disk)
storage.container: npz deflate for the pixel regions, torch.save (xb) for history/labels
storage.scale: uint8 -> float32 /255 happens only at load through vision.regions_to_batch
storage.hud: hud_score/hud_status are byte-identical across all 80 decisions (asserted per event); stored once as [1,3,H,W,C] and expanded to 80 rows at load, so the values are identical while the 80 redundant copies are not written
storage.why: a float32 copy of the same content is 4x larger and adds nothing: every consumer divides by 255 immediately

aux.task: from the GRU state predict whether the safe gap's screen-x centre lies left or right of x=192; label = round21.telegraph_gap(s), i.e. s.gap under s.mirror

aux.never_an_input: the label is a training-loss target only: it is not a pixel region, not a history field, not a feature channel, and no policy head tensor depends on it

equivalence.step0: unit tested: identical policy logits and identical masked action at step 0; perturbing the auxiliary parameters changes no policy logit

design.task: from the GRU state predict whether the safe gap's screen-x centre lies left or right of x=192; label = round21.telegraph_gap(s), i.e. s.gap under s.mirror
design.supervision: the rows whose logical frame 2*i lies inside round21.telegraph_window(s) = [wall_frame-45, wall_frame)
design.rows: the preview-window decisions only, for every event
design.seen: the stored round21 training features of the six F1 train events: exactly the rows the auxiliary loss trained on, so this is fit
design.holdout: the six F1 validation events, each replayed along that checkpoint's own stored closed-loop trajectory, re-rendered from its own x trace; the label scores the prediction and is never an input
design.chance: 0.5: the six labels are balanced 3/3 on both splits, so a majority baseline cannot beat chance
design.label_use: the label exists only inside the training loss and inside this scoring function; `PrivNetwork` (the closed loop) is the unmodified parent class and cannot read it

reference.note: round22 measured this target from the frozen 256-d trunk features at 0.985 and from its 94-d pooled vector at 0.674; the numbers here are about the GRU state, not the trunk features, so they are not comparable in level - they are comparable *between the two arms* of this round, which is the question being asked

design.target: binary: the gap's screen centre above x=192, i.e. the auxiliary label
design.rows: the preview-window decisions of the six F1 validation events, from the replay
design.fit: ridge on standardised inputs with an intercept, leave one geometry group out
design.caveat: 132 rows against 256 dimensions and a label that is constant within an event: the probe separates events as much as frames, so only the whole lambda sweep and the arm-to-arm comparison are read, never a single value

usage.note: one row per (network, F1 validation event); `aux_*` is the auxiliary head on the replayed pixels, `policy_*` is the stored closed loop of the same checkpoint; a high aux correctness with a low policy toward count is the "the task was learned, the behaviour did not use it" reading, cell by cell

prediction.note: the masked argmax actually taken, from the stored rows; per event over all 80 decisions and over the telegraph-window decisions only

base_bias.note: the frozen baseline (B0) is the policy head the residual offset is built on; its screen preference on the identical renders is the prior this round is testing against

probes.replay_note: every replay reports its own fidelity: the fraction of steps on which the rebuilt stack reproduces the stored masked argmax

round22_reference.decodability: round22 probe: 256-d trunk features 0.985 side accuracy on the held-out geometry (lambda sweep 0.953-0.985); the 94-d pooled vector 0.674
round22_reference.behaviour: round22: 95-97% of telegraph-window decisions are hold; every F1 death is on wall_frame; the fusion delta is 94.4% constant

comparison.note: three seed pairs, six F1 validation events each; X minus A; descriptive only

limitations: n=3 seeds and 7 validation groups; the 14 validation events collapse to 7 geometries because a mirror is not an independent sample, and F1 validation is 3 groups / 6 events

the auxiliary label is constant within an event and perfectly mirror-paired (3 left / 3 right on each split), so a head could in principle read "which world is this" instead of "where is the gap"; the per-cell table, the distance-from-centre column and the confusion are reported so that this cannot be hidden
the auxiliary task is supervised only on the six F1 train events and only inside the telegraph window, so 8 of the 14 update positions carry an exactly-zero auxiliary term
the auxiliary weight (0.5) is fixed before the run and never tuned
the F1 win condition is exact parking inside a 12-20 px gap; it is not tactical understanding
synthetic fixed-y worlds, two-frame actions, no shot, no bomb, no real TH08 pixels
a privileged training-time label is not a route to a deployable policy; research heads only: no formal gate, no deployable checkpoint, no game
